sources.name: NYT election results JSON (undocumented, 2026 LIVE)
sources.cost: Free, no auth, CORS open (access-control-allow-origin: *). ToS risk: undocumented, NYT ToS prohibits scraping/commercial reuse; gray area for personal dashboards.
sources.latency: Origin is a GCS bucket behind a CDN with cache-control max-age=5 and stale-while-revalidate=5. Last-modified was 00:18:19 GMT, 22s before my request, so it is updating every few seconds. Data is AP-sourced (provider field) plus NYT model estimates.
sources.granularity: Race level, down to county. reporting_units has levels state and county. NY governor file has 63 reporting units, including Dutchess (156 precincts total). House file has NY-17 and NY-18 with a Dutchess county row each (21 and 135 precincts). Per-unit fields: eevp (NYT estimated expected vote pct), precincts_reporting/total, total_votes, candidates[].votes.total, vote-type splits, called_by, winner_accepted_at.
sources.verified_live: YES, curled at about 7:18pm ET Nov 3 2026. HTTP 200. Sizes: senate 0.99MB (35 races), house 9.2MB (436 races), governor 0.8MB, results-new-york 1.4MB, results-new-york-governor 308KB. All counts were still 0 for NY because NY polls had not closed yet (9pm ET close). Not verified with real vote counts.
sources.notes: Patterns that 404: results-president (no presidential race in 2026), results-new-york-senate, results-ballot-measures, and 2022-dated paths. The 2024 file pages/data/2024-11-05/results-president.json still works (832KB), so the pages/data/{date}/results-{office|state}.json pattern is stable and good for test replays. The older api/ pattern (2020/data/api/2020-11-03/votes-remaining-page/national/president.json) still returns 200 (6.5MB). Each file also carries partyControlTimeseriesData and pollClosingTimes. Use If-None-Match/ETag to poll cheaply; poll every 10-30s and not faster. The house file is 9MB, so prefer the state-scoped file. NYT can change or block this at any time.

summary: The best find is the NYT undocumented JSON feed, which is live for the 2026 midterms. The pattern is https://static01.nyt.com/elections-assets/pages/data/2026-11-03/results-{senate|house|governor|new-york|new-york-governor}.json. I curled it at about 7:18pm ET and got HTTP 200, no auth, and CORS open. Headers show cache-control max-age=5 with a last-modified stamp 22s old, so the files refresh every few seconds. The data is AP-sourced and includes NYT model estimates. It goes down to county level: the NY governor file has 63 units, and Dutchess County rows exist in the governor race (156 precincts), NY-17 (21 precincts) and NY-18 (135 precincts). Vote counts were all 0 for NY when I checked, because NY polls had not closed (9pm ET), so real values are unverified. There is no presidential race this year, so results-president and results-ballot-measures return 404. ToS risk is real: it is undocumented, NYT's terms prohibit scraping and commercial reuse, and the files could be changed or blocked at any time. It is fine for a personal dashboard, but poll gently (10-30s, ETag) and credit NYT/AP. For CNN, Politico, WaPo, NBC and Fox I could not confirm a 2026 feed. My path guesses returned 404 or bot blocks (403/000), and web search only turned up 2016 and 2020 patterns. The next step there is to capture network requests in a real browser. The official AP Elections API (api.ap.org/v3/elections) responds 403 and needs a paid key, with no published pricing found. I did not examine Dutchess BOE results beyond confirming that elections.dutchessny.gov loads (200). A dashboard looks feasible: poll the NYT state-scoped files from a small server and render NY governor and House results by county."}
